title: General Rules of Succession in the Case of Males — Section 8 HSA

content.overview: Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 lays down the general rules of intestate succession to the property of a male Hindu. Property devolves first upon Class I heirs; failing them Class II; failing them agnates; failing them cognates, in that order.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Male Hindu intestate? (2) Separate property (not pure coparcenary interest under s. 6)? (3) Class I present? (4) Order: I → II → agnates → cognates?
content.study:
Section 8: the property of a male Hindu dying intestate devolves according to the provisions of Chapter II — (a) firstly, upon the heirs specified in Class I of the Schedule; (b) secondly, if no Class I heir, upon Class II heirs; (c) thirdly, if no Class I or II, upon agnates; (d) lastly, upon cognates.

Class I heirs take simultaneously and to the exclusion of others. Distribution among Class I is governed by ss. 9–10 and related rules.

Section 8 applies to separate property of a male Hindu. Coparcenary interest is first handled under s. 6; the share so ascertained then passes under the intestate scheme.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Order of devolution
sections.body: Class I → Class II → agnates → cognates.

sections.heading: Class I preference
sections.body: Class I heirs take simultaneously and exclude all others.

sections.heading: Separate property focus
sections.body: s. 8 is the general male intestate rule for property governed by the Act’s intestate chapter; coordinate with s. 6 for coparcenary interest.

sections.heading: Distribution
sections.body: Further distribution among simultaneous heirs is under ss. 9–10 and related provisions.

sections.heading: Contrast with female intestacy
sections.body: Succession to female Hindus is under ss. 15–16, not s. 8.

provisions.title: General rules of succession in the case of males

examples.title: Class I present
examples.body: Male Hindu dies intestate leaving widow and son — Class I take to the exclusion of Class II and remoter heirs.

hypotheticals.question: If Class I heirs exist, can Class II take any share under s. 8?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Class I take firstly and exclude Class II, agnates and cognates.

distinctions.title: s. 8 male intestacy vs s. 15 female intestacy
distinctions.right: Female Hindu — different order under ss. 15–16.

misconceptions.trap: s. 8 alone decides every Hindu succession problem including pure coparcenary interest.
misconceptions.correction: Coparcenary interest is first addressed under s. 6; s. 8 is the general male intestate order.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Order: Class I → Class II → agnates → cognates. Class I simultaneous and exclusive. Coordinate with s. 6 for coparcenary interest.
